title: Endothelialized Microfluidics for Studying Microvascular Interactions in Hematologic Diseases
protocol: Create a photomask by submitting a CAD drawing of the microfluidic device to an outside mask vendor.
Clean a bare silicon wafer with piranha solution (10:1 ratio of sulfuric acid and hydrogen peroxide) for 15 minutes.
Dip the cleaned wafer in hydrofluoric acid for 30 seconds.
Rinse the wafer with deionized water for approximately 10 seconds.
Spin Microchem SU-8 2025 photoresist onto the wafer to a height of 30 μm using a spin coater at 3000 rpm.
Place the wafer with SU-8 on a hotplate at 95 °C for 5 minutes to drive off excess solvent.
Expose the wafer to UV light (160 mJ/cm² measured at 365 nm) in a mask aligner after placing the mask over it.
Place the exposed wafer back on a hotplate at 95 °C for an additional 5 minutes to further accelerate polymerization of SU-8.
Immerse the wafer in SU-8 Developer, primarily composed of PGMEA, for 4 minutes to remove non-cross-linked SU-8.
Rinse the newly developed wafer with 100% isopropyl alcohol for 10 seconds.
Dry the wafer using pressurized nitrogen or allow it to evaporate in a clean fume hood.
Tape the edges of the dry wafer into a petri dish to prevent movement.
Apply 1 mL of Sigmacote to the wafer using a pipette.
Cover the wafer with the top of the petri dish and swirl to ensure complete coating.
Remove the cover and allow the wafer to dry until all solvent has evaporated.
Mix PDMS polymer and curing agent at a 10:1 ratio (w/w).
Remove air bubbles from the mixture using a vacuum desiccator.
Pour the mixture onto the wafer, approximately 5 mm thick.
Pour an additional amount of the mixture into a flat bottom dish to create a thin sheet of PDMS, approximately 1 mm thick.
Cure the poured PDMS at 60 °C in an oven overnight.
Cut out around the cured PDMS device using a knife or scalpel and remove it from the wafer.
Cut a thin sheet of PDMS slightly larger than the device.
Create inlet and outlet holes in the PDMS device using a 1.0 mm hole punch.
Clean the surfaces of the device and the sheet using scotch tape.
Expose the surfaces of the PDMS device and PDMS sheet to oxygen plasma for 30 seconds.
Connect smaller tubing to a small length of large tubing, which is then connected to a syringe with a blunt-point needle filled with fibronectin solution.
Insert the smaller tubing into the inlet of the PDMS microdevice.
Apply pressure to the syringe to fill the channels completely with fibronectin solution and create a 100 μL drop at the outlet port.
Incubate the device at 37 °C for 40-60 minutes.
Connect a fresh syringe filled with PBS to the blunt point needle.
Apply pressure to the syringe to rinse the device with PBS.
Prepare 1,000,000 cells/mL of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) in endothelial growth media with 8% dextran.
Connect the new syringe and tubing as specified, using approximately 1 meter of tubing.
Prevent any leaks or bubbles in the entire perfusion system to ensure successful seeding of endothelial cells.
Eliminate bubbles from the syringe and tubing before introducing cells into the microdevice.
Prime the entire perfusion system with cell solution before attaching the tubing to the microfluidic device.
Using a syringe pump, infuse cell suspension into PDMS device at a volumetric flow rate of 1.23 μl/min for 2 hours at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Ensure the syringe pump is at the same height as the PDMS device.
Use longer tubing for the inlet to ensure cells and media are adequately warmed before contacting the device.
Perfuse fresh growth media for 2-8 days at a ratio of 1.23 μl/min using the same syringe pump and long tubing.
Inject blood or cell suspension into the system for experimentation.
